summary: Extend the Vite + @insforge/ui dashboard (ui/src, 16 files, ~1.7k lines today) so it is the self-host console: an auth gate that detects local vs server mode from GET /me, a Setup page (first admin via POST /auth/signup then POST /auth/login), a Login page, an Account > API tokens page over GET/POST/DELETE /tokens that prints the exact `insta login --api-key` line, a two-lane Deploy dialog (image via POST /projects/:id/deploy, template via POST /projects/:id/template-deployments with a required/optional variable form and a step poller on GET /template-deployments/:id), a Templates gallery over GET /templates and GET /templates/:code, a service detail page with Settings (rename, always-on, cpu/memory limits, volume) and a Domains section over the cloud's compute/domain routes, and service rows that show hostnames, the Sleeping state from GET /projects/:id/runtime-health, a Wake button (POST .../start, compute only, as on the cloud) and an always-on toggle. Every network call maps to a route that exists in insta-platform (cited per route). Server-only UI is hidden in local mode; nothing in the dashboard wakes a sleeping service except an explicit Wake, so the console's own polling never holds services awake. All new helpers are pure .ts modules under ui/src/lib with vitest tests run from the root config; the daemon-side contract additions get fake-adapter tests in test/server.test.ts.

Extend Service with always_on?, image?, port?, volume_gib?, template_code?, template_logo_url? and redefine endpoint as a full URL (scheme included) for compute and host:port for databases while domain stays a bare host[:port] (cloud Service.domain). Add methods: me(), login(email,password), logout(), signup(email,password,name?), tokens(), createToken(name,expiresInDays?), revokeToken(id), templates(), template(code), deployTemplate(p,{templateCode,branch,variables}), templateDeployment(id), deployImage(p,{image,port,group,branch}), addService(p,{type,name,branch,public?,image?,port?,alwaysOn?,volumeGib?}) replacing addComputeService, runtimeHealth(p,branch), setAlwaysOn(p,sid,enabled), limits(p,sid), setLimits(p,sid,{memoryMb,cpu?}), dbInstance(p,branch), dbSettings(p,branch,{scaleToZero?,cpu?,memory?}), domains(p,branch,group), addDomain(p,{hostname,branch,group}), domainStatus(p,{hostname,branch,group}), removeDomain(p,{hostname,branch,group}). In call(): keep the 202 approval_required detection before the ok branch (a 202 template-deployment accept has no status:'approval_required' and falls through as ok); on status 401 and when location.pathname is not /login or /setup, call the registered onUnauthorized hook (set by AuthGate) instead of returning an error. Add apiUrlForCli() = origin with a leading 'console.' label replaced by 'api.', else origin.

Wrap Routes in <AuthGate> (new component). Add top-level routes /setup (Setup), /login (Login), /account/tokens (Tokens, inside a minimal AccountShell with a back link). Add project-scoped routes services/:sid (ServiceDetail) and templates (Templates). Home keeps the projects redirect; AuthGate decides before Home renders.

New. Calls api.me() once on mount and exposes {mode,user,refresh} through React context (useAuth()). Renders nothing until the answer arrives; mode 'setup' -> <Navigate to=/setup>, 'login' -> <Navigate to={`/login?next=${path}`}> unless already there, 'local'|'server' -> children. Registers api.onUnauthorized = () => setMode('login').

New. First-run page (server mode only; if useAuth().mode !== 'setup' redirect to /). Form: email, password (min 8, matching the cloud's schema), confirm password, optional name. Submit: POST /auth/signup then POST /auth/login; then step 2 'Create a CLI token' (inline TokenCreate component with name prefilled 'laptop') showing the one-time key and the exact `insta login --api-key <key> --api-url <apiUrlForCli()>` line with CopyButton; 'Go to dashboard' -> refresh() then navigate('/').

New. Email + password form over POST /auth/login; on 200 refresh() and navigate(safeNext ?? '/'); 401 -> 'Wrong email or password.'; 403 -> message from body. Mirrors the console AuthShell layout (title, subtitle, centered card) without OAuth buttons.

New. Account > API tokens: table (name, prefix + bullets, created, last used, expires) from GET /tokens filtered !revokedAt; create row (name input, optional expiry Select 30/90/365/never) -> POST /tokens -> one-time reveal panel (key, CopyButton, the `insta login --api-key` line); revoke via ConfirmDialog -> DELETE /tokens/:id. Reuses TokenCreate from components/TokenCreate.tsx (shared with Setup).
New. The create + reveal widget used by Setup and Tokens.

TopBar: replace the static 'local' label with mode-aware identity: local -> 'local'; server -> user.email with a DropdownMenu (API tokens -> /account/tokens, Sign out -> POST /auth/logout then navigate /login). SideBar: add SideItem Templates (lucide LayoutTemplate) under the branch section after Service. Keep the daemon health dot.

Replace StatusDot(runtime) with StatusCell({row, health, waking, onWake}) rendering the derived ServiceStatus (lib/status.ts): Online, Sleeping (+ Wake button for compute), Stopped, Suspended, Starting/Waking (spinner), Crashed, Not deployed, unknown. Add HostLink({domain, endpoint}) rendering the bare hostname with an external link when endpoint starts with http, plus CopyButton. Add TemplateLogo({src}) with fallback tile. Keep Modal, Chip, ErrorNote, TypeIcon.

Header gains a primary 'Deploy' button (opens DeployDialog) next to 'Add Service'. Row columns: Service (TypeIcon or template logo, name; click navigates to services/:sid), Status (StatusCell from runtime-health merged by serviceId), URL (HostLink), Always on (Switch for compute and managed rows; postgres row's switch drives database/settings scaleToZero), Updated, kebab. Kebab: compute Start/Stop/Suspend/Restart/Rename/Remove; storage Make public/private; postgres and managed rows: Remove (server route now allows it per project-parity WP) and Rename for managed. Poll: services and runtime-health every 5 s, 2 s while any service is waking. Empty state when services.length===0. Replace AddDialog with components/AddServiceDialog.tsx.

New (moved out of Services.tsx). Type Select (postgres, storage, compute, redis, mysql, mongodb), name Input (lower-kebab validation), compute extras: image (optional), port (default 8080), Always on Switch (default off), Volume Switch + size (Gi); storage extra: Public Switch. Submits POST /projects/:id/services with branch = current branch. 409 -> 'name already used'.

New. Tabs Image | Template. Image lane: image (required), port (number, default 8080), target Select (existing compute services + 'New service' with a name input) -> POST /projects/:id/deploy {image, port, group, branch}; 202 approval -> ApprovalPrompt retry. Template lane: TemplatePicker (search + category rail + rows) -> TemplateDeployForm (variables) -> POST template-deployments -> DeploymentProgress (step list + per-service states + urls + error/logsTail). Opened from Services and from Templates (preselected code).

New. Renders required then optional (collapsed 'Optional (N)') variables per lib/templateVars.ts rules; secret-looking names as password inputs with reveal; disabled Deploy until canSubmit; server 400 missing_variables marks fields.

New. Polls GET /template-deployments/:id every 2 s (CLI cadence) until status in succeeded|failed|partial or 15 min; renders the four steps (create services, write variables, deploy, health check) with done/active/pending marks, services list with state badges and URL links, error and logsTail in a <pre>.

New. Gallery: SearchInput, category rail (categories derived from the list, 'all' first, counts), card grid (logo, name, tagline, category Badge, version, license). Card click opens TemplateDetailDialog: name, tagline, upstream links, services summary (name, type, port, volume, alwaysOn), variables (required/optional with descriptions), readme via components/Markdown.tsx, footer 'Deploy to <branch>' -> DeployDialog template lane with the code preselected. Data via GET /templates (one-shot, 60 s poll) and GET /templates/:code on open.
New, dependency-free (about 80 lines): headings, paragraphs, fenced code, inline code, bold, links (rel=noreferrer, http(s) only), unordered/ordered lists; raw HTML is escaped, never rendered.

New. Route services/:sid. Header: TypeIcon/logo, name, StatusCell with Wake, HostLink. Tabs (Tabs/Tab as in Logs.tsx): Overview (image, port, volume, desired state, template code, last update; compute only shows Restart) and Settings. Settings sections: General (rename via POST .../rename), Sleep (Always on Switch: compute/managed -> PUT .../always-on; postgres -> PATCH /database/settings {scaleToZero: !enabled}, read from GET /database/instance), Resources (compute/managed: cpu and memory inputs bounded by cap from GET .../limits, Save -> PUT .../limits; postgres: cpu/memory quantity inputs -> PATCH /database/settings {cpu,memory}, read cpuMilli/memoryMib from /database/instance), Volume (read-only size from GET .../volume; grow via PUT), Domains (compute only, components/DomainsSection.tsx; hidden when GET compute/domains answers 501), Danger (Remove service, gated service.remove).

New. List from GET /projects/:id/compute/domains?branch&group; Add dialog (hostname Input validated by the cloud's HOSTNAME_RE, POST compute/domain, gated deploy -> ApprovalPrompt); per-domain card: hostname, stage badge (lib/domains.ts), hint line, DNS records table (type, name, value, CopyButton), Verify (GET compute/domain?hostname), Remove (ConfirmDialog, DELETE compute/domain).

When any of the three reads fails with status 503 and message matching /sleeping/, stop polling (usePoll enabled=false) and render EmptyState 'Postgres is sleeping' with copy: wakes on the next connection; turn on Always on in the service settings to keep it warm; button 'Service settings' -> services/pg-db. Resume polling on 'Check again'.

No route change (docker logs of a stopped container do not wake it). Add a muted note when runtime-health says standby for the selected component: 'Sleeping; showing the last lines before it went to sleep.'

Copy only: 'its own Postgres (data forked at the file level), its own bucket (objects copied), and a redeploy of every app; a new environment starts asleep unless a service is always on.' No em dashes.

usePoll gains an options bag {intervalMs, enabled} (enabled=false skips the fetch and timer; keeps data). Add useWaking(): a Map<serviceId, startedAt> with wake(sid) and a derived anyWaking flag; entries clear when health reports healthy or crashed, or after 60 s.
New pure module: deriveStatus(row: Service, health?: RuntimeHealthRow, waking?: boolean): ServiceStatus. Rules in the algorithm section.
New pure module: flattenVariables(detail), isSecretName(name), canSubmit(vars, values), payloadVariables(values) (drops empty strings), applyMissing(body) for the 400 missing_variables shape.
New pure module: domainStage(result) -> 'active'|'verifying'|'needs-records'|'error'; HOSTNAME_RE; normalizeHostInput(raw).
New pure module: apiUrlForCli(origin: string): string; cliLoginLine(key, origin).

sharedSurface.config:
Read by the daemon, not the SPA (the SPA infers everything from routes and location):
- INSTA_OSS_MODE=local|server (default local; server when INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN is set). Server mode turns on the auth gate, /auth/* and /tokens, cookie sessions.
- INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN: install domain; api.<domain> and console.<domain> both route to the daemon's fastify listener (router WP), so the SPA stays same-origin. The SPA derives the CLI api url from its own origin (console. -> api.).
- INSTA_OSS_UI_DIST (exists, src/server.ts:671).
- INSTA_OSS_ALWAYS_ON_DEFAULT (default false): the alwaysOn used when POST /services or a template omit it; the Add Service dialog sends alwaysOn explicitly so the knob only affects CLI/template callers.
- INSTA_OSS_SESSION_TTL_HOURS (default 720) for the cookie/session expiry; the SPA handles a 401 by returning to /login.
- ui/vite.config.ts VITE_INSTA_API (exists) for dev proxying.
sharedSurface.engineSeams:
Functions the dashboard calls through server.ts (owner WP in brackets; this WP only consumes them):
- engine.services(projectId, branch): emit always_on, image, port, template_code, template_logo_url, bare domain + URL endpoint [router WP + project-parity WP].
- engine.runtimeHealth(projectId, branch): standby vs crashed via sleptAt; 'starting' during wake [scheduler WP].
- engine.lifecycle(projectId, sid, 'start', branch): the Wake door; clears desiredState stop intent and sleptAt, calls scheduler.wake (which may evict under RAM pressure) [scheduler WP]. Compute only, as the cloud (openapi.yaml:5264 'Start a compute service').
- engine.setAlwaysOn(projectId, sid, enabled, branch?) -> { service } for compute and managed; engine.dbSettings(projectId, {scaleToZero}, branch) persists dbAlwaysOn; engine.dbInstance echoes scaleToZero and cpuMilli/memoryMib [scheduler WP].
- engine.serviceLimits(projectId, sid) -> { limits, cap, volume? } and engine.setServiceLimits(projectId, sid, {memoryMb, cpu?}) -> { service, limits, cap }; cap = host cpu count and total RAM rounded to 256 MB; memoryMb must be a multiple of 256 (cloud rule) [scheduler WP].
- engine.listDomains/addDomain/domainStatus/removeDomain(projectId, {hostname, branch, group}) -> DomainResult [router WP]; 501 in local mode so the SPA hides the section.
- engine.templatesList(query?, category?), templateDetail(code), deployTemplate(projectId, {templateCode, branch, variables, deploymentId?}), templateDeployment(id) [templates WP].
- engine.addService(projectId, {type, name, branch, public, image, port, alwaysOn, volumeGib}) replacing fixedService for postgres/storage [project-parity WP].
- engine.dbMetricsSnapshot/dbActivity/dbQueryStats/dbInsight: when the branch database is asleep throw Error('database is sleeping: it wakes on the next connection') and do NOT wake; server maps 'sleeping' -> 503 [scheduler WP]. runtimeMetrics/runtimeLogs read docker and never wake.
- server.ts: auth preHandler (identity WP) exempts /healthz, /auth/*, /api/auth/*, /templates, /templates/:code (public on the cloud, platform server.ts:2614 security: []), and static/SPA paths; isApiPath extended; the router's HTTP lane must not stamp activity for api./console. hosts.

algorithm:
A. Boot and mode detection (AuthGate, api.me)
1. On first render AuthGate calls GET /me with the browser's cookies (same origin, fetch default credentials). Map: 200 with user.id === 'local' -> mode 'local'; 200 otherwise -> mode 'server' with user; 401 and body.error starts with 'setup required' -> 'setup'; any other 401 -> 'login'; network failure -> the existing 'daemon unreachable' CenterNote.
2. mode 'setup' -> Navigate /setup (replace). mode 'login' -> Navigate `/login?next=<encoded pathname+search>` unless pathname is /login or /setup. Otherwise render children. The context value {mode, user, refresh} is read by Layout (TopBar), Setup, Login, Tokens, Services (server-only affordances).
3. api.call: after fetch, if res.status === 401 and pathname not in {/login,/setup}, invoke api.onUnauthorized() (AuthGate sets mode 'login', which triggers the redirect) and still return {kind:'error',status:401}. Never redirect on 401 from /auth/login itself (wrong password).
4. Local mode never shows Setup, Login, Tokens, the user menu or the Domains section; the Services always-on switches and Sleeping states still render (the scheduler runs in local mode too).

B. Setup page
1. Guard: if useAuth().mode !== 'setup' -> Navigate '/'.
2. Form validation client-side: email non-empty and contains '@'; password length >= 8 (cloud minLength, openapi.yaml:2434); confirm === password. Submit disabled otherwise.
3. Submit: r1 = POST /auth/signup {email, password, name?}. 403 -> show 'An admin already exists. Sign in instead.' with a link to /login. 400 -> body.error. 200 -> r2 = POST /auth/login {email, password}; on 200 the cookie is set by the response; call refresh() (re-runs GET /me) and move to step 2.
4. Step 2 'Create a CLI token' embeds TokenCreate with name default 'laptop'. POST /tokens {name} -> 201 {token, record}. Show token once in a monospace box with CopyButton, and the line `insta login --api-key <token> --api-url <apiUrlForCli(location.origin)>` with its own CopyButton. Note: 'This key is shown once.' 'Skip' and 'Open dashboard' both navigate('/').
5. apiUrlForCli(origin): parse URL; if hostname starts with 'console.' replace that label with 'api.' and keep protocol and port; else return origin unchanged (local mode, raw IP). Pure, unit-tested.

C. Login page
1. Fields email, password; submit -> POST /auth/login. 200 -> refresh() then navigate(safeNext) where safeNext = next param only if it starts with '/' and not '//' else '/'. 401 -> 'Wrong email or password.' 403/other -> body.error. Enter key submits.
2. A 'First run? Create the admin' link appears only when GET /me answered setup required (mode 'setup'); otherwise not shown.

D. Tokens page (/account/tokens)
1. Guard: mode must be 'server' (local -> Navigate '/').
2. usePoll(api.tokens, [], 30000). Rows: tokens.filter(t => !t.revokedAt) sorted by createdAt desc. Columns: name; `${prefix}••••••••`; relTime(createdAt); lastUsedAt ? relTime : 'never'; expiresAt ? date : 'never'.
3. Create: name required (trim), optional expiry Select (30, 90, 365 days, never) -> POST /tokens {name, expiresInDays?}. On 201 render the reveal panel (same as Setup step 2) and reload the list. 400 -> error under the input.
4. Revoke: kebab -> ConfirmDialog 'Revoking <name> immediately breaks anything using it.' -> DELETE /tokens/:id -> reload. 404 -> 'Already revoked.' then reload.

E. Sign out (TopBar menu)
POST /auth/logout {} -> regardless of result, navigate('/login') and call refresh(); the daemon clears the cookie.

F. Services page
1. Data: services = usePoll(api.services(p,branch)), health = usePoll(api.runtimeHealth(p,branch)); both intervalMs = anyWaking ? 2000 : 5000. Index health by serviceId.
2. deriveStatus(row, h, waking) (ui/src/lib/status.ts), evaluated in this order:
   a. waking -> {kind:'waking', label:'Waking'} (spinner).
   b. no h or h.status === 'unknown' -> if row.runtime is 'online' -> online, else unknown ('—').
   c. h.status 'healthy' -> online (green dot 'Online').
   d. h.status 'starting' -> starting (spinner 'Starting').
   e. h.status 'crashed' -> crashed (destructive 'Crashed', title 'Not answering on its port; check Logs').
   f. h.status 'none' -> none ('Not deployed').
   g. h.status 'standby': if row.type === 'compute' and row.desired_state === 'stopped' -> stopped ('Stopped'); if row.desired_state === 'suspended' -> suspended ('Suspended'); else sleeping ('Sleeping', muted dot, title 'Idle; wakes on the next request' for compute, 'Idle; wakes on the next connection' for databases). wakeable = kind === 'sleeping' && row.type === 'compute'.
   Storage rows have no health row (cloud omits storage) -> show '—' unless row.runtime given (today's field), then Online/Stopped.
3. Wake: the Wake button (compute + sleeping only, per the cloud's start route) calls POST .../start?branch=; on ok: waking.wake(sid) (records Date.now()); on approval -> ApprovalPrompt with retry; on error -> ErrorNote. useWaking clears an entry when the next health read says healthy or crashed, or when Date.now() - startedAt > 60000 (the router's hold bound). Database rows show no Wake button; their Sleeping label says wakes on connect.
4. URL column: HostLink shows row.domain (bare host[:port]); if row.endpoint matches /^https?:\/\// render as <a href target=_blank rel=noreferrer>; else plain text; CopyButton copies endpoint when present else domain. For a sleeping compute service the link keeps working (the router wakes on request); tooltip says so.
5. Always on column: compute and managed rows render <Switch checked={!!row.always_on}> -> PUT .../always-on {enabled}; on ok reload; 202 -> ApprovalPrompt (the cloud route is ungated, the daemon keeps it ungated; the handler is still written through the approval-aware path). Postgres row: Switch checked = !dbInstance.scaleToZero (usePoll(api.dbInstance(p,branch), 15000)); disabled until the instance read lands (console db-scale-to-zero-row.tsx:40-61); toggle -> PATCH /database/settings?branch= {scaleToZero: !checked} -> reload. Storage: no switch.
6. Row kebab: compute: Start/Stop/Suspend when online else Start; Restart (POST .../restart, gated deploy); Rename; Remove (X). Managed: Rename, Remove. Postgres: Remove (only when the project has more than one postgres? No: the daemon decides; the UI shows Remove and surfaces 409/501 messages). Storage: Make Public/Private, Remove.
7. Header: 'Deploy' (primary) opens DeployDialog; 'Add Service' (secondary) opens AddServiceDialog. Empty state when services.length === 0: 'No services yet. Add a database or storage, or deploy an app or a template.'
8. Row click (name cell) -> navigate(`services/${row.id}`).

G. Service detail page (services/:sid)
1. Find the row in api.services; 404 -> back to the list. Header: name, StatusCell with Wake, HostLink, template badge when template_code.
2. Tabs Overview | Settings (Tabs/Tab from @insforge/ui as in Logs.tsx:55-58).
3. Settings > General: name Input + Save -> POST .../rename {name}; 409 shown inline.
4. Settings > Sleep: Switch 'Always on' with hint 'Never put to sleep when idle. Off: sleeps after the idle window and wakes on the next request (compute) or connection (databases).' Same calls as F.5. For compute with desired_state 'stopped' the hint adds 'This service is stopped; Start it to re-enable wake on request.'
5. Settings > Resources (compute and managed): usePoll(api.limits(p,sid), 30000) -> inputs cpu (integer 1..cap.cpu) and memory (MB, step 256, 256..cap.memoryMb); a caption 'This machine: <cap.cpu> vCPU, <cap.memoryMb> MB'. Save -> PUT .../limits {memoryMb, cpu}; validation before send: memoryMb % 256 === 0, cpu >= 1; 400 shown inline; 202 -> ApprovalPrompt. Postgres: inputs cpu (vCPU, string like '2') and memory ('4Gi') from dbInstance.cpuMilli/1000 and memoryMib/1024 -> PATCH /database/settings {cpu, memory}.
6. Settings > Volume: GET .../volume -> 'sizeGib Gi mounted at mountPath'; grow input -> PUT .../volume {sizeGib} (grow-only; 400 inline). 404 -> 'No volume' with 'Attach' (PUT with a size).
7. Settings > Domains (compute only): on mount GET /compute/domains?branch&group. 501 -> hide the whole section (local mode); 404 -> treat as empty. Add: hostname normalized (lowercase, strip scheme/path/trailing dot) and validated by the cloud's rule /^(?=.{1,253}$)([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}$/ -> POST /compute/domain {hostname, branch, group}; 202 -> ApprovalPrompt retry; 409 -> body.error ('already attached'). Card per item: hostname, stage badge from domainStage(r): r.status === 'error' or r.errorReason -> 'error'; r.configured && r.status === 'active' && no dns[].status in {missing, mismatch} -> 'active'; some dns[].status === 'ok' or r.ssl === 'pending' -> 'verifying'; else 'needs-records'. Hints: active 'Serving over HTTPS.'; verifying 'Records found. The certificate is being issued; click Verify to re-check.'; needs-records 'Create the DNS records below at your DNS provider, then click Verify.'; error r.errorReason. DNS table rows: type, name, value (CopyButton each). Verify -> GET /compute/domain?hostname&branch&group -> replace the card's result; toast-like inline note when the stage changes. Remove -> ConfirmDialog -> DELETE /compute/domain {hostname, branch, group} -> reload.

H. Deploy dialog
1. Tabs Image | Template; both submit into the current URL branch.
2. Image lane: image Input (required, trimmed), port Input (number, default 8080), target Select listing compute rows plus 'New service…' which reveals a name Input (lower-kebab). Submit -> POST /projects/:id/deploy {image, port, group, branch}. Result ok -> close, reload services, and mark the group waking (the container is starting). 202 approval -> ApprovalPrompt with retry(submit). 400 -> inline error.
3. Template lane, phase 1 (pick): TemplatePicker over GET /templates: SearchInput filters client-side on code, name, tagline, tags (the fields the cloud's ?query matches, console templates.ts:282-290); category rail lists 'all' plus categories present in the query-filtered set with counts. Row click -> GET /templates/:code -> phase 2.
4. Phase 2 (form) uses lib/templateVars.ts: flattenVariables(detail) = [...detail.variables.required.map(v=>({...v,required:true})), ...detail.variables.optional.map(v=>({...v,required:false}))] de-duplicated by name (first wins, required OR-ed), the CLI's rule (template-manifest.ts:206-224). For each variable: mustFill = required && generate == null && default === undefined. Render required group first, optional group collapsed as 'Optional (N)'. Input placeholder: generate ? 'generated on deploy' : default !== undefined ? `default: ${default}` : ''. isSecretName(name) = /(PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN|_KEY$|API_KEY|PRIVATE)/.test(name) -> type=password with an eye toggle. canSubmit(vars, values) = every mustFill var has values[name].trim() !== ''. payloadVariables(values) drops keys whose trimmed value is '' (the platform treats blank as absent; templates/scripts/variables-lib.mjs:14-20, CLI template.ts:153-165).
5. Submit -> POST /projects/:id/template-deployments {templateCode, branch, variables}. Responses: 202 with status 'approval_required' -> ApprovalPrompt retry(submit) (gates may chain: service.add, secrets.write, deploy; each retry may 202 again with a new action until accepted). 202 with deploymentId -> phase 3. 400 with error === 'missing_variables' -> mark each missing[].name (or .key) as required-empty and keep the form. 409 -> inline body.error (in progress, copy cap). 404 -> 'Template not found.'
6. Phase 3 DeploymentProgress: poll GET /template-deployments/:id every 2000 ms (CLI cadence, template.ts:302) until status in {succeeded, failed, partial} or 15 min. stepIndex = ['create_services','write_variables','deploy','health_check'].indexOf(step); mark steps < stepIndex done, stepIndex active, rest pending; succeeded marks all done. Services list: name, state badge (pending/created/deployed muted; healthy success; failed destructive), url link when present. failed/partial: show error and logsTail in a scrollable <pre>. Buttons: 'Close' (always), 'Open service' when exactly one service has a url. On close reload services and mark the new groups waking if health is not yet healthy.
7. The dialog is also opened from Templates with {templateCode} preselected: it jumps straight to phase 2.

I. Templates gallery page (/p/:projectId/:branch/templates)
1. usePoll(api.templates, [], 60000) (one fetch per minute; the catalog is static locally). Search and category as in H.3. Grid of cards: TemplateLogo(logoUrl) with a fallback tile (first letter), name, tagline (line-clamp 2), Badge category label (map: ai-agent -> 'AI agent', otherwise the raw value with dashes to spaces), version, license when not null.
2. Card click -> GET /templates/:code -> TemplateDetailDialog: header (logo, name, tagline, maintainer, version, links: upstream repo, documentationUrl), Services table (name, type, image, port, volume yes/no, always on yes/no) from the services map, Variables (required with descriptions; optional collapsed), README rendered by components/Markdown.tsx (raw HTML escaped), footer 'Deploy to <branch>' -> DeployDialog(templateCode).
3. Sidebar item 'Templates' after 'Service'.

J. Add Service dialog
1. Type Select default 'compute'. Name Input validated /^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,37}[a-z0-9])?$/ (the cloud's lower-kebab, max 39). compute: image (optional), port (default 8080, only when image set), Always on Switch (default off, hint 'Off: sleeps when idle and wakes on request'), Volume Switch + size Gi (default 1). storage: Public Switch. postgres/redis/mysql/mongodb: name only.
2. Submit -> POST /projects/:id/services {type, name, branch, ...(compute: image?, port?, alwaysOn, volumeGib?), ...(storage: public)}. 201 -> close, reload. 202 -> ApprovalPrompt retry. 409 -> 'A <type> named <name> already exists.' 400 -> body.error (for example the per-type cap).

K. Database page sleeping state
1. The three reads keep their intervals (10/10/15 s). When a read fails with status 503 and /sleeping/i.test(message): set sleeping=true, disable all three polls (usePoll enabled=false), render EmptyState (icon Moon) 'Postgres is sleeping' + body 'It wakes on the next connection. Turn on Always on in the service settings to keep it warm.' + buttons 'Service settings' (navigate services/pg-db) and 'Check again' (re-enable polls once).
2. Nothing on this page wakes the database; the daemon's observability reads never wake (engine seam).

L. Visibility matrix (mode -> shown)
local: Services, Environments, Templates, Deploy, Add Service, ServiceDetail (Domains hidden after 501), Sleeping/Wake, Always on, Logs, Database, Secrets, Approvals, Operations, Usage, Settings. Hidden: Setup, Login, Tokens, user menu.
server: everything above plus Setup (once), Login, /account/tokens, user menu, Domains.

M. Routing and static serving
1. SPA client routes added: /setup, /login, /account/tokens, /p/:projectId/:branch/templates, /p/:projectId/:branch/services/:sid. None collides with an API prefix: isApiPath (src/server.ts:672-673) matches exact '/tokens' or '/tokens/…', so '/account/tokens' falls to index.html; '/auth', '/api', '/templates', '/template-deployments' must be added to isApiPath so a browser hitting /templates gets JSON as on the cloud (the SPA gallery lives under /p/…/templates).
2. ui/vite.config.ts API_PREFIXES gains '/auth', '/api', '/templates', '/template-deployments', '/regions'. Dev cookie flow works because the proxy is same host (localhost) and the daemon sets Secure only over https.
3. Fetches stay same-origin with default credentials; no Authorization header is ever stored in the browser (the session is the HttpOnly cookie), so the SPA holds no secret except a just-minted token shown once.

N. Polling and sleep interaction (invariant)
The dashboard's periodic reads are: /orgs/local/projects, /branches, /services, /runtime-health, /approvals, /healthz, /secrets/tree, /operations, /events, /policy, /logs, /metrics, /database/*, /tokens, /templates. All are answered from state.json, docker ps/logs/stats, or a 503 sleeping answer; none passes through a router lane, so an open dashboard tab never keeps a service awake. Only Wake (POST start), Deploy, template deploy, Restart, and clicking a service URL wake anything.

Build gate: `npm run build:ui` (tsc --noEmit + vite build) stays green; no new runtime dependency in ui/package.json (Markdown renderer is hand-written; Switch, Tabs, Select, Badge, CopyButton, ConfirmDialog, SearchInput, Skeleton, EmptyState all exist in @insforge/ui 0.1.7 exports).

Docker integration (integrator only, never run by parallel implementers): none owned by this WP. The public e2e step 'setup page and token login' is a curl script: POST /auth/signup, POST /auth/login (capture cookie), POST /tokens, `insta login --api-key … --api-url https://api.<domain>`, `insta status`. A browser-level check of the dashboard is a later playwright step, not in v1.
risks: Setup-vs-login discrimination rides on the 401 error text of GET /me ('setup required'); it is daemon-internal on both ends and pinned by a contract test, but any rewording breaks first-run. Alternative considered: a server-side redirect of '/' to '/setup' from the SPA fallback; rejected because the SPA cannot then distinguish after client-side navigation.

POST /auth/signup answering 200 {} relies on 'status' being optional in the cloud schema (platform server.ts:634 Type.Optional). If the reconciler prefers { status: 'verification_sent' } for byte parity, the Setup page must not read it either way (it does not).

Cookie sessions on a cloud API surface: the cloud's actor() reads only Bearer (platform server.ts:299-307). Accepting an HttpOnly cookie is a daemon-internal addition; CSRF exposure is bounded by SameSite=Lax plus JSON bodies (cross-site simple requests cannot carry application/json without a preflight), but the identity WP must reject state-changing requests whose Origin header is present and not the console origin.

The daemon's `endpoint` field changes meaning for compute (today host:port without scheme, src/engine.ts:465; target full URL). It is a dashboard-only additive field, but any script reading it breaks; the reconciler should confirm no CLI/MCP consumer.

Wake is compute-only because the cloud's start route is compute-only (openapi.yaml:5264). Users may expect a Wake on a sleeping Postgres row; the dashboard says 'wakes on the next connection' and offers Always on. If Tony wants a DB wake button, the only contract-clean door is making a database read a wake door, which contradicts the 'observability never wakes' rule.

The Database page shows a sleeping empty state instead of live signals; until the scheduler WP lands the 503 'sleeping' answer, the page keeps polling a stopped container and shows a 502 error (today's obsCode, src/server.ts:84).

Custom-domain UX depends on the router WP's DomainResult fields (dns[].status, ssl, errorReason). If the edge reports nothing per record, every domain renders as 'needs-records' until configured flips; acceptable, and the Verify button re-reads.

Templates gallery logos: recommending data: URIs in logoUrl (schema says 'absolute https URL') is a shape nuance the templates WP owns; the UI handles null and any URL, so the fallback tile covers the worst case.

Multiple postgres/storage per project (decision 6) means the dashboard can no longer assume ids 'pg-db' and 'st-store' (today src/engine.ts:434, 440; DatabaseInsight links to services/pg-db). The Database page must pick the first postgres row from /services when there are several; a per-service database picker is deferred to #18.

Polling load: Services page issues two reads every 5 s (2 s while waking) plus TopBar/SideBar polls; on a 2 GiB VPS this is negligible, but the state.ts write lock (spec, src/state.ts:31-37) must not serialize reads behind router stamps.

ApprovalPrompt retry loops for template deploys can chain three gates (service.add, secrets.write, deploy); each grant is one-shot, so a user who closes the prompt mid-chain leaves a consumed grant and must retry the deploy; matches the CLI's behaviour.
openQuestions: Should GET /templates and GET /templates/:code stay public in server mode (cloud: security: [], platform server.ts:2614/2638) or be behind the session like every other route per spec section 2? Recommendation: public, matching the cloud; nothing sensitive is in the catalog.
Always-on switch label: mirror the console's inverse 'Scale to zero' switch (service-settings.tsx:161-187) or the CLI verb 'always-on'? Design uses 'Always on'; a one-line change either way.

Should the Add Service dialog default Always on to off (serverless by default on one node) while the cloud defaults compute to always-on (services.ts:98-99, INSTA_COMPUTE_ALWAYS_ON_DEFAULT)? Design sends the switch value explicitly and defaults off; confirm with the scheduler WP's INSTA_OSS_ALWAYS_ON_DEFAULT.

Local mode hostnames: does `domain` carry a port ('web-shop-main.localhost:8080') or does the router bind a privileged port so domains are bare? The UI treats domain as opaque host[:port] either way; the manifest parity question belongs to the router WP.

Does the reconciler want the plural GET /projects/:id/compute/domains (cloud route table only, hidden from openapi, platform server.ts:2797) in the fixed route list? Without it the Domains section cannot enumerate on load (the console hit this as #292).
Token expiry: cloud POST /tokens accepts expiresInDays; should the self-host default be 'never' (design) or a finite default?

Should the postgres row expose limits through PATCH /database/settings {cpu, memory} in v1 (design includes it, read from cpuMilli/memoryMib on /database/instance), or only compute/managed via /limits?

UI test runner placement: run ui/src/lib tests from the root vitest config (design, no new dependency) versus adding vitest to ui/package.json; the former needs the root tsconfig/eslint to include ui/src/lib/*.ts.
